newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Japan, NZ avoid confrontation in nuclear waste row.
newsitem.headline: Japan, NZ avoid confrontation in nuclear waste row.

text.p: The prime ministers of Japan and New Zealand avoided confrontation in a row over Japanese nuclear waste shipments passing through the Tasman Sea during 1-1/2 hours of talks on Wednesday.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and his New Zealand counterpart, Jim Bolger, clearly stated their nations' positions on the issue but did not go into details, a Japanese Foreign Ministry official said.

Wellington has opposed Japanese nuclear waste shipments passing through the Tasman Sea on its way between Japan and France. The recycled waste is shipped back to Japan after being reprocessed in France.
New Zealand espouses a strong anti-nuclear stance and passed legislation in the mid 1980s banning nuclear-powered and nuclear-armed vessels from its ports.
Hashimoto said he and Bolger had also discussed domestic reforms.

"If I could tell you the most effective piece of advice I got, it was that when most of the mass media thinks that although the prime minister is saying he'll enact reforms, he probably can't -- that is the best time to carry through reforms," he told a news conference.
Hashimoto has pledged sweeping reforms, including trimming government agencies down to size and reducing the budget deficit.
Some critics, however, question how bold he can be given his long-standing ties to bureaucrats.
New Zealand, which went through two phases of radical reforms in the early 1980s and 1990s to unwind a virtual command economy, is now struggling to find a model for a private pension scheme.
Japan is also under pressure to reform its pension policies, given its rapidly ageing population and low birth rate.

Hashimoto, whose visit here is the last leg of a diplomatic swing which has taken him to Washington and Canberra, also expressed Japan's support for New Zealand's entry into the fledgling Asia Europe Meeting (ASEM) which links 10 Asian nations with the 15 members of the European Union.
Hashimoto leaves for Tokyo on Wednesday evening.
